title: Describe the Previous Line
statement:
The **look-and-say** sequence of texts starts with `"1"`. Every next text **describes the previous one** by reading its runs of equal digits from left to right and writing, for each run, the **length of the run** followed by the **digit**. So `"1"` is described as "one 1" = `"11"`; `"11"` as "two 1s" = `"21"`; `"21"` as "one 2, one 1" = `"1211"`; and so on.

Return the `n`-th text of the sequence (the first one is `"1"`).

hints.nudge: To produce each text you only need the previous one. How do you read it run by run?
hints.pattern: Start with the text 1 and repeat n - 1 times: scan the current text, count the length of each run of equal digits and build the next text from (count, digit) pairs.
hints.pseudocode:
text = "1"
repeat n - 1 times:
  next = empty; i = 0
  while i < len(text): j = i; while j < len(text) and text[j] == text[i]: j += 1
    append (j - i) then text[i] to next; i = j
  text = next
return text
hints.walkthrough: The definition is itself a recursion (the n-th text is the description of the (n - 1)-th), but an iterative loop avoids deep calls. To describe a text, walk through it with an index i. For the digit at i, move a second index j to the end of the run of equal digits; the run length is j - i. Append that length and then the digit, and continue from j. The texts grow by about 30% each time (the 30th has 4,462 digits), so building them by appending to a string builder is fast enough. Digits in the text are only 1, 2 and 3 (a run never has more than three equal digits), so the run length is always a single digit.
